{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -c 1
#   -p priority
#   -t 2-00:00
#   --mem 4G
#   -o logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake_%A.log
#   -e logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake_%A.log

#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=48h

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem 4G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: -p priority (partition)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different priority/limits, affecting wait time and throughput.

# Omitted Slurm options: -o/-e with %A token (array/master job id)
# Slurm's %A token is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

module unload python
module load gcc conda2 slurm-drmaa/1.1.1
conda activate rctest

# The Snakemake DRMAA string targets Slurm (e.g., -p/--mem/-t/-o/-e/-J).
# Flux does not accept Slurm DRMAA options; omit --drmaa and run locally within the allocation.
# Performance implication: the workflow will not submit each rule as a separate scheduled job;
# it will execute within this one Flux allocation, which can reduce cluster utilization and increase walltime.

snakemake \
  --snakefile src/20_62_nonallelespec_rc-test-Snakefile.py \
  --jobs 9980 \
  --restart-times 0 \
  --cluster-config config/rc-test-snakemake-cluster.json \
  --latency-wait 120

conda deactivate
"
}
